open_points.subject: Project-overview failure classification
open_points.text: “the project overview answers a failed part as `temporarily_unavailable` with no value” does not define which failures count as a failed part, while the same convention maps Registry, persistence and storage failures to 502 or 500
open_points.question: Which failures during an already-authorized overview are converted into a component-level `temporarily_unavailable`, and which still fail the whole request?
options: Convert any required read-dependency failure, including Registry and persistence failures, into `temporarily_unavailable` for the affected component
Convert only explicitly enumerated dependency failures; propagate all others through the normal HTTP error policy
Convert every exception raised while building a component into `temporarily_unavailable`
open_points.default_guess: Convert expected Registry and persistence read failures into component unavailability, but propagate programming, validation and invariant failures.

witness.initial: A staff member is authorized to read an active project, and the project guard's Registry validation has succeeded.
events: The staff member requests the project overview.
The portal-store read for the active budget raises `PersistenceError`.
outcomes: The route returns HTTP 200 with `budget_availability = temporarily_unavailable`, no budget value, and any other readable components.
The normal failure policy applies and the entire request returns HTTP 500 with no overview.

open_points.subject: Propagation of a shared dependency failure across overview parts
open_points.text: “a failed part” and “Each of the six parts gets its own availability” do not state how a failure of data shared by several parts affects their separate availability values
open_points.question: When one failed read or calculation supplies several overview components, which components must become `temporarily_unavailable`, and may the shared dependency be read independently again for another component?
options: Mark every component that depends on the failed shared input unavailable
Mark only the component whose builder encountered the failure and let other builders perform their own reads
Fail the whole overview when a shared dependency cannot be obtained
open_points.default_guess: Read shared inputs once and mark every dependent component unavailable, while continuing independent components.

witness.initial: An authorized project has an active budget, expenses, progress and payments; all four views require active-budget facts directly or for derived fields.
events: The first read of the active budget fails transiently.
outcomes: Budget, expense, progress and payment components are all `temporarily_unavailable`; photos remain available.
Only budget is `temporarily_unavailable`; later component builders read independently and return expense, progress and payment values.
